calls.head: The Sabres come in rested
calls.body: The Blue Jackets played last night and get no rest before this one. Teams in that spot usually get the worse of the chances, so we expect the Sabres to control more of the play than they usually do.

calls.head: Where the Blue Jackets have the edge: forecheck pressure
calls.body: The Blue Jackets are near the top of the league for forecheck pressure, and the Sabres are around the middle. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Blue Jackets put more forecheck pressure on than the Sabres.

surprises.head: Columbus got the good looks
surprises.body: Columbus’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 10.5% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.5% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 150 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: Buffalo brought the hits
surprises.body: Buffalo usually hits less than most teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 157 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 88 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

story.head: Power has three assists as the Sabres take down the Blue Jackets
paras: Jack Quinn got the scoring started for the Sabres early in the first, but Kent Johnson made it 1-1 for Columbus late in the period. Josh Norris put the Sabres back ahead 2-1 just over two minutes later. Rasmus Dahlin extended the lead to 3-1 early in the second, and Norris scored again midway through the period to make it 4-1. Josh Doan stretched the lead to 5-1 just over a minute later, and the goal stood after the Blue Jackets challenged for goalie interference. The Jackets’ Sean Monahan left in the second period and didn’t return. The next day, he was ruled out with a lower-body injury. Zach Werenski made a dent in Buffalo’s lead on the power play with less than two minutes left, bringing it to 5-2. Owen Power finished with three assists.

The Sabres had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Blue Jackets 37-26. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made 24 saves for the Sabres, and Jet Greaves stopped 32 of 37 at the other end. The Sabres improved to 8-5-3 and climbed to sixth in the Atlantic, while the Blue Jackets fell to 7-8-0, sixth in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Kent Johnson has a point in seven straight games.
Josh Doan scored again against Columbus, and has seven goals in eight games against them since 2023-24.
Steven Lorentz made his Blue Jackets debut, after two seasons with the Maple Leafs.
The season series is even at 1-1.
